mt-037-reich-process.notes: Steve Reich, essay written 1968, in Writings on Music 1965–2000, Oxford 2004, pp. 34–36; primary statement of Reich aesthetics, not a rule for all process composition.

mt-037-omt-pop-modules.title: Form in Pop/Rock Music: Formal Containers and Module Structures
mt-037-omt-pop-modules.notes: Sections Formal Containers, Module boundaries, Module Structures; style-scoped examples of timbral, dynamic, melodic, and harmonic section markers.

mt-037-ardour-import.title: Ardour Manual: Adding Pre-existing Material
mt-037-ardour-import.notes: Official Ardour manual, Session > Import, Region List and drag-drop to editor; tool behavior only, not mixing outcome.

mt-038-mcadams-grouping.title: A Taxonomy of Orchestral Grouping Effects Derived from Principles of Auditory Perception
mt-038-mcadams-grouping.notes: Stephen McAdams, Meghan Goodchild and Kit Soden, Music Theory Online 28(3), 2022, DOI 10.30535/mto.28.3.6. Full text: paragraphs [3.2],[3.7],[4.1],[5.1],[5.5],[6.2] and Examples 2/12/22; hypothesis-based account of orchestral grouping, not a test of our scores.

mt-038-rimsky-orchestration.title: Principles of Orchestration (Steinberg-edited, 1922 English edition)
mt-038-rimsky-orchestration.notes: Nikolay Rimsky-Korsakov; editor Maximilian Steinberg; translator Edward Agate. Prefaces and Volume I, Chapters I–II and doubling subsections. A historically situated perspective, not a physical or cross-cultural universal.

mt-038-phil-flute.title: Philharmonia Orchestra: Flute
mt-038-phil-flute.notes: Instrument guide, Range. C4 normal lowest note, optional B-foot B3; piccolo sounds one octave higher than written.

mt-038-phil-violin.title: Philharmonia Orchestra: Violin
mt-038-phil-violin.notes: Instrument guide, Range and Bowing. G3 D4 A4 E5 string tuning, timbre varies with string choice at a given pitch; bow direction and articulation discussed.

mt-038-phil-cello.title: Philharmonia Orchestra: Cello
mt-038-phil-cello.notes: Instrument guide, Introduction, Range and Bowing; C G D A open-string tunings, low-to-high melodic roles, bowing variation, sul C / sul G.

mt-038-phil-bass.title: Philharmonia Orchestra: Double Bass
mt-038-phil-bass.notes: Instrument guide, Range; instrument sounds an octave below written and standard sounding open strings E1 A1 D2 G2.

mt-038-phil-horn.title: Philharmonia Orchestra: Horn
mt-038-phil-horn.notes: Instrument guide, Introduction. Describes long sustained inner harmony as common horn role alongside powerful tutti passages. Descriptive repertoire practice, not universal range/loudness rule.

mt-038-phil-trumpet.title: Philharmonia Orchestra: Trumpet
mt-038-phil-trumpet.notes: Instrument guide, Introduction: muted lyrical passages and bright, forceful projection among possible roles.

mt-038-goodchild-oxford.title: Perceptual Processes in Orchestration
mt-038-goodchild-oxford.notes: Meghan Goodchild and Stephen McAdams, The Oxford Handbook of Timbre, pp. 496–524; publisher abstract accessible. Background corroboration only; precise grouping claims grounded in the freely accessible 2022 MTO full text.

mt-038-dawdreamer.title: DawDreamer User Guide
mt-038-dawdreamer.notes: Overview and Basic Workflow; RenderEngine, processor graphs, automation, offline rendering. Does not validate acoustic instrument realism.

mt-038-dawdreamer-render.title: DawDreamer Render Engine and BPM
mt-038-dawdreamer-render.notes: Rendering audio by time or beats, loading processor graphs, retrieving rendered samples.

mt-038-ardour-automation.title: Ardour Manual: Automation
mt-038-ardour-automation.notes: Fader, trim, mute, pan and processor automation. Describes capabilities not mixing outcomes.

mt-038-ardour-pan.title: Ardour Manual: Panning
mt-038-ardour-pan.notes: Panning for mono/stereo and multi-channel outputs; practical capability rather than perceptual guarantee.

mt-039-gotham-exposition.title: High Baroque Fugal Exposition
mt-039-gotham-exposition.author: Mark Gotham
mt-039-gotham-exposition.notes: Open Music Theory 2nd ed. II Counterpoint and Galant Schemas, section High Baroque Fugal Exposition. Direct locators: Basic Definitions; Structure / Voice Entries; Subject; Answer; Countersubject; Free Counterpoint; Links; Example (BWV 847 mm. 1-9). Author Mark Gotham credited on chapter. Source for period-specific terminology, not the original note events of this lecture.

mt-039-hutchinson-analysis.title: Music Theory for the 21st-Century Classroom, 30.8 Fugue Analysis
mt-039-hutchinson-analysis.author: Robert Hutchinson
mt-039-hutchinson-analysis.notes: Section 30.8 and Figures 30.8.1–30.8.4, BWV 847. Definitions of subject, answers, exposition/episode, bridge, two regular countersubjects, additional free counterpoint, subject-head fragmentation; distinguish from the original Bach source.

mt-039-ku-counterpoint.title: University of Kansas School of Music: Counterpoint
mt-039-ku-counterpoint.author: University of Kansas School of Music
mt-039-ku-counterpoint.notes: Terminology list and Fugues—Sample Questions; includes real and tonal answers, invertible counterpoint, episode, stretto, double fugue, canon; pedagogical conventions, not a claim that every fugue contains every device.

mt-039-ucsb-rothfarb.title: Music 103 Counterpoint Course: Invertible Counterpoint and Fugue
mt-039-ucsb-rothfarb.author: David Rothfarb, University of California Santa Barbara
mt-039-ucsb-rothfarb.notes: Distinct linked sections Invertible Counterpoint (Discussion and examples) and Fugue (Subject and Answer, Exposition and model fugues). Useful for pedagogy and planning, not an empirical validation of this original score.

mt-039-bach-wtc1.title: Das wohltemperierte Klavier I, BWV 846–869 — Manuscripts and editions
mt-039-bach-wtc1.author: Johann Sebastian Bach; score and source metadata cataloged by IMSLP contributors
mt-039-bach-wtc1.notes: Movement list for 24 prelude-fugue pairs; includes Prelude and Fugue in C minor BWV 847 and links to manuscript sources/editions. Historical score attribution separate from modern analyses and recordings; no score copied into this pack.

mt-039-renwick-thesis.title: Voice-Leading Patterns in the Fugal Expositions of J. S. Bach’s Well-Tempered Clavier
mt-039-renwick-thesis.author: William Jonathan Michael Renwick
mt-039-renwick-thesis.notes: CUNY Graduate Center dissertation landing page; Abstract paragraphs on contrapuntal imitation and voice-leading patterns, 43 non-modulating subjects, three primary paradigms; do not assert detailed results beyond visible abstract.

mt-039-renwick-1991.title: Structural Patterns in Fugue Subjects and Fugal Expositions
mt-039-renwick-1991.author: William Renwick
mt-039-renwick-1991.notes: Music Theory Spectrum 13(2) (Fall 1991), pp. 197–218. Abstract describes subject paradigms, linear progressions and recurring expositions. No specific uninspected passages or formulae asserted.

mt-039-minnesota-composing.title: Composing a Fugue
mt-039-minnesota-composing.author: University of Minnesota Libraries Publishing
mt-039-minnesota-composing.notes: Exposition and real/tonal answer definitions visible in indexed search extract; direct full page inaccessible (403) in this pass. Use Gotham/Hutchinson as inspectable corroboration for detailed claims.

mt-040-schoenberg-biblio.title: Arnold Schoenberg, Fundamentals of Musical Composition (ed. Gerald Strang with Leonard Stein, Faber 1967): National Library of New Zealand catalogue
mt-040-schoenberg-biblio.notes: Authenticates title, editors, publisher, date. Does not furnish open full text or independently verify every passage. Chapters III–V cited from table of contents; no copyrighted score/text reproduced.

mt-040-frisch.title: Walter Frisch, The Early Works of Arnold Schoenberg, 1893–1908 (University of California Press, 1993), chapter 8 and note on motivic generative power
mt-040-frisch.notes: Open monograph; chapter 8 discussion of motives and Schoenberg compositional exercises, with reference to 1967 Fundamentals pp.64–67. Secondary scholarly corroboration of motivic pedagogy, not source of this lecture score.

mt-040-caplin-functions.title: William E. Caplin, Classical Form: A Theory of Formal Functions for the Instrumental Music of Haydn, Mozart, and Beethoven (Oxford, 1998), Chapter 1
mt-040-caplin-functions.notes: Original chapter 1, Some Basic Formal Functions: An Overview. Source for historical scope of formal functions and roles, not a classification of our original piece. PDF bibliographic title corroborated by Oxford University Press book.

mt-040-caplin-sentence.title: William E. Caplin, Classical Form (Oxford University Press, 1998), Chapter 3: Sentence, pp.35–48
mt-040-caplin-sentence.notes: Publisher abstract describing presentation, continuation and cadential functions of Classical sentence, with scope limited to Haydn/Mozart/Beethoven repertoire. DOI 10.1093/oso/9780195104806.003.0004.

mt-040-margulis.title: Elizabeth Hellmuth Margulis, On Repeat: How Music Plays the Mind (Oxford University Press, 2013/2014)
mt-040-margulis.notes: Publisher book abstract and chapters 1 (The Puzzle of Musical Repetition, pp.1–25) and 3 (Attention, Temporality, and Music that Repeats Itself, pp.55–74). Not experimental evidence about this lecture score.

mt-040-margulis-attention.title: Elizabeth Hellmuth Margulis, On Repeat (2013), Chapter 3: Attention, Temporality, and Music that Repeats Itself, pp.55–74
mt-040-margulis-attention.notes: Publisher abstract describes attention-oriented theories of repetition. Supports only general hypothesis that repetition affects temporal attention; no predicted preference for our score.

mt-040-huron.title: David Huron, Sweet Anticipation: Music and the Psychology of Expectation (MIT Press, 2006)
mt-040-huron.notes: Publisher description identifies a psychological theory of musical expectations and distinctions among response mechanisms; no quantitative prediction about these original bars.

mt-040-mcadams.title: Stephen McAdams, Meghan Goodchild, and Kit Soden (2022), A Taxonomy of Orchestral Grouping Effects Derived from Principles of Auditory Perception, Music Theory Online 28(3)
mt-040-mcadams.notes: Article abstract paragraphs on concurrent blending, sequential segregation, and segmental boundary-making. No experimental evaluation of the original oscillator piece.

mt-040-ardour-automation.title: Ardour Manual, Automation
mt-040-ardour-automation.notes: Track fader, trim, mute, pan and plugin-parameter automation; refer to introductory feature list.

mt-040-ardour-stems.title: Ardour Manual, Stem Exports
mt-040-ardour-stems.notes: Explains exporting independent track/bus files with silence to preserve synchronization and optional track processing. Does not promise plugin-equivalent cross-DAW reproduction.

mt-040-ardour-import.title: Ardour Manual, Adding Pre-existing Material
mt-040-ardour-import.notes: Documents import dialog and drag/drop of audio or MIDI into sessions.

mt-040-ardour-loudness.title: Ardour Manual, Loudness Analyzer and Normalizer
mt-040-ardour-loudness.notes: Documents peak/true-peak/integrated loudness analysis and gain normalization; source for practical level-check workflow, not a guarantee of rigorous perceptual loudness matching.

mt-040-dawdreamer-guide.title: DawDreamer maintainers, User Guide: RenderEngine, processors, graphs, parameter automation
mt-040-dawdreamer-guide.notes: Source for graph construction, rendering and audio retrieval. This lecture does not include an executed DawDreamer graph.

mt-040-dawdreamer-plugins.title: DawDreamer maintainers, Plugin Processor User Guide: State Management and Rendering
mt-040-dawdreamer-plugins.notes: Documents plugin processor, `load_state`, `save_state`, render interactions and per-plugin headless limitations; source for reproducibility cautions.
